ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the PEP lists maintained by the People's Bank of China (PBOC), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the domestic sanctions list of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Enhanced due diligence is required for any individual identified as a PEP, including verification of source of funds and wealth, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a real-time basis during the relationship, and upon any change in ownership or control. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years. Failure to identify a sanctioned entity or PEP may result in severe penalties under the AML Law and PBOC Order No. 3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and the SAMR Online Registration Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Chinese characters, with an optional English name. The Chinese name must consist of a trade name, a business description, and a legal form suffix (e.g., '有限公司'). Transliteration of foreign names must follow the standard pinyin system, and the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. Four-tier naming conventions apply: administrative division, trade name, industry description, and legal form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the local SAMR within 15 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written explanation of why the name should be approved, along with supporting evidence such as trademark registrations or prior use. The SAMR must respond within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the People's Court within 6 months. It is advisable to consult with a local corporate attorney to prepare a robust appeal, as the grounds for rejection are often based on similarity or prohibited tokens.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture in China. The company must maintain a physical registered office within the jurisdiction, which must be a real, rentable office space. Tax authorities and banks require a physical presence for verification and ongoing compliance. A virtual office may be rejected during company registration, bank account opening, or tax registration, leading to delays or penalties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1) Registered address must be a genuine office with a visible company nameplate; 2) Business license must be displayed; 3) Financial records and accounting books must be accessible; 4) Employees or a designated representative must be present during business hours. Risk: Moderate to high, especially for newly formed entities. Unannounced inspections by SAMR and tax authorities occur periodically, and failure to meet physical presence requirements can result in fines or revocation of the business license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), applicable Articles 14-18, 22-30, 31-38, 47-51 and 63-71; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Article 30 and the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List); Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Subjects (2022), Chapter II
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Administration for Market Regulation (Enterprise Registration Division) at the company's registered address
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company (Company Establishment Registration Application) filed on the integrated enterprise registration service platform
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital is imposed for a foreign-invested advertising-technology service company. The registered capital and shareholder contribution schedule must be set out in the Articles of Association. Unless the Articles provide an earlier date, the shareholders must pay their subscribed capital in full within five years of establishment. There is no blocked escrow account rule under general company law; however, foreign-currency contributions must be received through a licensed bank in China after completion of SAFE foreign-direct-investment registration, and the contributions must be recorded in the company accounts for statutory capital contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, effective upon issuance of the business license of CN_JV_LTD (the Company), that the Board of Directors (the Board) ratifies and accepts the certificate of incorporation, business license, unified social credit code, Articles of Association, shareholders agreement and all ancillary formation documents, and directs the legal representative to maintain the statutory registers, seal ledger, share-transfer records, minutes, financial records and corporate books at the registered office. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company and the subscriptions made by each shareholder for their respective equity interests are approved, adopted, ratified and confirmed; each shareholder shall contribute the subscribed capital on the schedule set out in the Articles, such schedule not exceeding five years from establishment unless lawfully extended; management is directed to open a capital receipt account, collect all contributions through lawful banking channels, retain all bank entry evidence and foreign-exchange admission documents, and obtain any additional capital verification or legal documentation required to evidence payment. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be at the address stated in the Articles, such address being adopted as the registered office for statutory service, and the Board authorises management to execute, deliver, register and administer the lease, building nameplate, service-of-process arrangement and any subsequent relocation filings with the Administration for Market Regulation. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed legal representative and chairperson of the Company, [Name] is appointed general manager, [Name] is appointed supervisor, and [Name] is appointed financial officer, each to serve until the first annual general meeting or until earlier removal; the legal representative shall have authority to sign, certify and submit all documents to government authorities and to execute contracts and bank instructions within the Board-approved limits. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open a RMB basic deposit account, a foreign-currency capital account and any ancillary accounts with [Bank Name]; the bank is authorised to honour and pay all cheques, drafts, SWIFT wires, ACH transfers, online banking instructions, foreign-exchange purchase orders and account documentation signed by the legal representative or by any two designated co-signatories whose specimen signatures have been submitted; and the Board approves the corporate seal, finance seal, contract seal and legal representative seal and authorises the legal representative to maintain custody and use them in accordance with the seal-control policy. RESOLVED, that each officer of the Company is authorised and directed to prepare, execute, file and deliver any notices, registrations, tax forms, foreign-exchange forms, banking forms, social insurance registrations, statistical returns and ancillary instruments needed to carry out the foregoing resolutions, and any such action already taken before the date of this resolution is ratified and confirmed. This resolution may be executed in counterparts and is effective immediately and remains in full force until amended or revoked by a later resolution of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Approval and Enterprise Registration Portal Intake
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Registration Division through the provincial one-stop enterprise registration service or the SAMR municipal service hall
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit an application for pre-approval of the company name on the integrated enterprise registration portal or at the local Administration for Market Regulation service window. The application must identify the proposed legal name, business scope, registered capital, nature of the entity, shareholder names, nationalities and domiciles. The registry will search the national enterprise-name database and reject a name that is identical, deceptive, prohibited or confusingly similar to a protected mark. If the name is approved, retain the returned name-approval notice because it must be attached to the establishment registration application. If the requirement to submit a negative-list declaration applies, confirm that the advertising-technology business is not on the restricted or prohibited list before filing.
required_dossiers: Completed company name pre-approval application form
Government-issued identity document or passport copy of each shareholder or investor
Certificate of incorporation and director register of each foreign corporate shareholder
Power of attorney appointing the local agent or incorporation filer
Statement of proposed business scope and registered capital
Contact information of legal representative and supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name pre-approval is rejected or queried, prepare a new name variant and immediately resubmit through the same portal; if the rejection is based on legal error, file an administrative reconsideration application to the superior SAMR within 60 days, or alternatively accept the query notice and amend the proposed name and business scope before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Legalisation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaries and Chinese consular legalisation service for foreign shareholder documents; local notary office for individual domestic shareholder signatures; no enterprise registry filing at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association, shareholder subscription schedule, board appointment letters, supervisor appointment letter and legal representative appointment certificate. Each foreign shareholder must obtain the necessary corporate authorisation or board resolution to invest in China, and the investor documents must be notarised, apostilled or consular legalised as required by the Chinese authorities, with certified Chinese translation prepared by a qualified translator. The Articles must state the company name, registered office, business scope, registered capital, contribution amounts and timeline, shareholder voting rights, board or executive director authority, legal representative appointment, supervisor powers, transfer restrictions, dividend distribution, dissolution and dispute resolution. After execution, preserve original signing pages for physical submission to the registry and scanned electronic copies for the one-stop portal. This step is crucial because the registry will not accept a foreign document submitted in raw foreign language without legalisation and translation.
required_dossiers: Drafted Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Shareholder subscription and capital contribution schedule
Board resolution of each foreign corporate shareholder authorising the investment and signatories
Notarised and consular legalised certificate of incorporation and good standing certificate of foreign shareholders
Power of attorney appointing the legal representative or local agent
Certificate of appointment of directors, supervisor and legal representative
Identity documents of all officers
Office lease agreement and property ownership certificate or landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or its intake system rejects the constitutional dossier for deficient legalisation or translation, correct the affected document and re-legalise or re-translate it and resubmit; if notarisation is questioned, have the signing shareholder send a fresh notarised signature and explanation letter; the five-day SLA restarts only after complete documents are accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Registration Division through the integrated establishment application platform or physical service hall
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete establishment registration package through the SAMR integrated enterprise establishment platform or at the service hall. The system will concurrently collect business registration, tax information, social insurance basics, personnel registration and, if applicable, import or export record information. After the platform validates the name approval, Articles, shareholder qualification, office address, capital schedule and officer appointments, the registry performs a legal form and substantive legality examination. On approval, the registry issues the business license with a unique unified social credit code. The company may lawfully commence activities only after the license is issued and, where necessary, after the enterprise seal is engraved and bank accounts are opened. No government registration fee is charged.
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration application form signed by all shareholder appointees
Name pre-approval notice
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Office lease, property ownership certificate of the landlord or premise-use certificate
Identity document of legal representative and all directors or executive director
Identity document of supervisor and financial officer
Capital contribution schedule and source-of-funds statement
Shareholder qualification evidence and legalisation files from Step 2
Negative-list self-declaration and foreign investment information report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query notice or correction demand, respond in writing within the prescribed period, normally 15 days, by amending the affected item and re-uploading; if the registration is refused, the shareholders may apply for administrative reconsideration to the supervising Administration for Market Regulation within 60 days, or initiate administrative litigation within six months, or simply cure the stated deficiency and file a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seal Engraving, Bank Account Opening and SAFE Foreign Direct Investment Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-authorised seal engraving enterprise; licensed commercial bank branch; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) registration through the bank (FDI basic information registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After license issuance, engrave the company seal, financial seal, contract seal and legal representative seal at a public security authorized engraving unit, and record the seal specimens with the public security authority. Then open a RMB basic deposit account and a foreign-currency capital account at a licensed bank. The bank will collect beneficial ownership and AML/KYC information, specimen signatures, shareholder identity and source-of-funds declarations. If foreign investors remit capital into China, the bank will initiate the FDI registration on the SAFE online foreign exchange platform and issue a foreign exchange business registration notice. After the bank account is activated, shareholder capital contributions may be paid, but the funds must be used only for lawful business purposes and cannot be withdrawn or converted inconsistently with the foreign exchange rules. No physical industrial permit is involved.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code certificate
Seal engraving certificate or public security seal-record receipt
Official company seal, financial seal, contract seal and legal representative seal
Legal representative passport or national identity document and specimen signature
Board banking resolution and minutes
Shareholder identification documents and proof of foreign legal existence
Articles of Association and capital contribution schedule
FDI foreign exchange basic information registration form
Office lease and business-address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE queries the account opening or FDI registration, provide the requested beneficial ownership, source of funds, background of investors, lease invoice, and corrected constitutional documents; if the foreign exchange registration is suspended, coordinate with the bank to update the SAFE system and file an amendment within the applicable period, preserving all correspondence for audit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Tax, Social Insurance and Ancillary Digital Service Compliance Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (local tax service hall or e-tax platform); local human resources and social security bureau; local statistics office and, only if a website or app is operated, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology for internet information service filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete or confirm all post-formation registration duties. The tax registration is usually completed together with business registration through the one-stop system, but validate that the unified social credit code, taxpayer status, tax identification, legal representative and accounting records are correctly loaded in the e-tax portal. Complete social insurance, housing fund, statistical registration, payroll plan and any work-committee registration if the company has employees. For a digital advertising exchange platform, assess whether the actual service operation triggers an administrative internet information service filing (ICP filing) or value-added telecom licence; the payload indicates no statutory licence is mandated, so the entity should only obtain the filing if the factual operation of websites or apps requires it. Confirm that no environmental impact assessment, civil defense fire permit or industrial operating licence is needed because the entity has no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activities.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code certificate
Tax registration or taxpayer registration data from the one-stop system
Legal representative and financial officer identity documents
Social insurance registration forms and employee list
Office lease contract and property tax payment records
Financial accounting system registration and bank account certificate
Digital platform factual description and conclusion on ICP filing if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social insurance registration is missing or mismatched, visit the local tax bureau or social insurance window with the business license and legal representative authorisation to double-register; if the ICP filing is rejected, correct the domain registration, hosting company and applicant data and resubmit before the domain is publicly used; no industrial or environmental cure is relevant because none of those permits applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital advertising technology and programmatic ad exchange service; no industrial licensing authority has jurisdiction over the entity under ISIC 7310.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no operating, manufacturing, assembling, chemical or warehousing permit applies. The entity will hold only a general business license and, if operationally necessary for a website or app, an administrative internet information service filing; no industrial operating licence is triggered.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment would be the review agency only for construction projects; this digital service does not reach any EIA category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no environmental registration, screening form or full environmental impact report is required because the activity is an office-based software and advertising platform operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no production wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, hazardous waste storage or atmospheric discharges; only ordinary office water usage and municipal solid waste, with no quantitative environmental discharge thresholds applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no civil defense fire acceptance certificate, structural load inspection or industrial work-safety approval applies to an office-only digital service company. Standard fire-prevention duties and portable fire extinguisher compliance under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China remain applicable to the leased office premises, and the landlord must maintain the building fire-fighting acceptance certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online portals: Unified National Electronic Tax Bureau (etax.chinatax.gov.cn) and the National Electronic Invoice Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Sino-foreign equity JV is incorporated with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and receives an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). The USCC is automatically transmitted to the STA through the one-stop market incorporation and tax registration procedure, and the same USCC becomes the entity's TIN, VAT ID and employer registration number. After incorporation, the JV must complete online tax registration in the Unified National Electronic Tax Bureau, activate its electronic tax filing credential, and obtain the tax-control / e-invoice authorization. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Chinese establishment, the non-resident contractor must obtain a non-resident TIN via temporary tax registration at the district STA in charge of the Chinese withholding agent or payor, supplying a certificate of foreign incorporation, foreign tax residence certificate, contract and China-source income explanation; alternatively, the Chinese counterparty may register the non-resident for withholding purposes. No separate VAT ID exists; the USCC is used for VAT and all national tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or a standalone hybrid mismatch election. An entity's classification as a resident enterprise is mandatory under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. The only elective indirect tax mechanism is voluntary general VAT taxpayer registration for small-scale taxpayers with sound accounting and a fixed place of business.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable VAT turnover triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; below that, the taxpayer remains a small-scale VAT taxpayer unless it voluntarily elects general VAT taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates real-time e-invoicing under the STA Golden Tax Phase IV framework. All VAT invoices, especially special VAT invoices for B2B supplies, must be issued through the National Electronic Invoice Service Platform or through ERP software integrated via STA-certified APIs. Invoices carry a unique digital signature, invoice code and QR code; issuance, voiding, red-letter offsetting and reconciliation are reported to the STA in real time. The system performs automated anti-fraud cross-checks against customs declarations, tax returns, bank receipts and non-resident payment records. The applicable service VAT rate for the AdTech/SSP entity is 6%, while the general goods/import VAT rate remains 13%.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the PRC export tax refund (exemption) regime, 0% VAT with input VAT credit applies to physical export of goods and to enumerated cross-border services (including R&D, design, contract energy management, software services, information system services, business process management services and offshore service outsourcing) provided to an overseas recipient and wholly consumed outside China. Pure advertising placement or agency services are generally VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated; however, the programmatic SSP/DSP platform can qualify as a zero-rated software/information system service if the contract, delivery and usage evidence demonstrate that the service is provided to an overseas client and wholly consumed offshore, and the corresponding foreign exchange is repatriated within the statutory period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form approved by China Customs
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical goods
Export Sales Contract and Purchase Order
Bank Receipt of Export Proceeds / Foreign Exchange Income Declaration
VAT Special Invoices for purchased inputs for refund calculation
Cross-border service agreement and offshore consumption certificate for services
Geolocation and electronic delivery logs for digital/SSP services
Foreign exchange credit advice and payment confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and refund claims are jointly audited by the STA and China Customs. If the required customs, delivery, offshore-consumption or foreign-exchange repatriation documents are missing, false or inconsistent, the STA will deny the 0% treatment, claw back the refunded VAT, impose a late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and assess administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of the improper refund. Intentional false declarations constitute the criminal offense of fraudulently obtaining export tax refunds under Article 204 of the PRC Criminal Law, punishable by fines of one to five times the defrauded amount and imprisonment. The taxpayer's credit rating will be downgraded, triggering revocation of paperless and fast-track export-refund facilitation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), with the People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the central bank authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi is convertible for current-account transactions, including goods trade, services and ordinary corporate remittances, but capital-account transactions remain tightly controlled by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. For a Sino-foreign equity joint venture, inbound equity capital must enter through an FDI foreign-exchange capital account after SAFE registration, and the foreign currency may be settled into RMB only when the bank is satisfied as to the genuine underlying transaction. Outbound profit remittances are lawful after the annual statutory audit, tax clearance and a board-approved distribution, but the bank will require audited financial statements, booking vouchers, certificates of tax filing and the joint venture's distribution resolution. Export proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic foreign-exchange account or sold to a designated bank on the strength of customs or service-transaction records. No fixed surrender ratio is currently imposed; the true constraint is documentary authenticity and registration. Convertibility risk is concentrated in capital-account items such as early repayment of foreign-shareholder loans, equity transfers and liquidation remittances, each of which demands a separate SAFE filing or approval before funds can leave.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds for goods must be repatriated into China within 180 days after customs export declaration and must be received onshore or into a designated foreign-exchange account; the exporter may retain the full amount in foreign currency or sell part/all to the bank at the prevailing market rate, as no statutory mandatory conversion ratio is in force. For service-export flows, including programmatic advertising, platform or SSP fees, the bank reviews the service contract, the VAT/service invoice and platform settlement statement, and the proceeds should be received within the time limit set by SAFE and bank policy; there is no forced conversion ratio, but every receipt is subject to transaction authenticity and electronic reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Settlement Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Account plus General Operational Settlement Account
Capital Injection Escrow/Settlement Account and Cross-Border RMB Operating Account
Foreign Currency Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW, not viable as a principal account. Foreign fintech EMIs without a PBOC banking license cannot open an RMB or foreign-currency corporate settlement account for a mainland-domiciled JV, cannot receive FDI capital injections, cannot be linked to SAFE tax or VAT filings, and cannot support statutory capital verification. The JV may use PBOC-licensed third-party payment institutions for domestic small-value collections or disbursements, but those are not bank accounts and cannot carry cross-border corporate treasury flows. Any blueprint that relies on an offshore digital EMI as the operating treasury vehicle would fail account opening, SAFE registration and audit requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative must appear in person at the tier-1 bank branch for a face-to-face KYC interview when opening the FDI foreign-exchange capital account and the main operating account; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for first-time capital account onboarding in mainland China. Foreign shareholders may execute a notarised and legalised power of attorney abroad, and original notarised or apostilled corporate documents, passports, board resolutions and source-of-funds evidence must be presented. For routine RMB operational accounts, some banks permit video interviews only after the legal representative has already established identity in-person at the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered address is a virtual office or shared agency address with no visible local operations, and the JV may be flagged as a shell entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original business license, physical lease or ownership certificate, floor plan and office photographs, employee social insurance contribution records, payroll and labour contracts, board minutes approving premises, utility bills, annual tax returns, and an invitation for the bank to conduct an on-site inspection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity automated ad bid and settlement flows involving many low-value payments to multiple overseas SSPs or media vendors, triggering abnormal transaction monitoring and possible layering indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Programmatic platform service agreements with each SSP/DSP, KYB onboarding records and sanctions screening results, aggregated monthly invoices by counterparty, bid request and auction log samples, proof of gross vs net settlement, media vendor reconciliation statements, end-to-end data flow diagrams, and an external audit letter on internal financial controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected misuse of FDI equity capital, such as same-day onward transfers or intra-group shareholder loans immediately after foreign currency settlement to RMB.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved capital utilisation plan, signed contracts and VAT-inclusive invoices for planned expenditures, monthly cash-flow forecast, bank account authority matrix with dual-approval requirements, certified accountant capital verification report after each injection, statutory ledger entries, and a treasury compliance undertaking signed by the legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Overseas media inventory or publisher counterparties located in OFAC, EU, UN or other high-risk sanctioned jurisdictions, creating sanctions and proliferation-financing exposure for the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions, PEP and adverse-news screening outputs for all active counterparties, jurisdiction risk matrix with country-by-country commercial rationale, geo-blocking and inventory denial controls for prohibited jurisdictions, contractual zero-tolerance sanctions representations, the JV AML/CTF and sanctions compliance policy, and an annual external AML audit report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investors must remit share capital from their own offshore bank accounts into the JV's designated FDI foreign-exchange capital account opened at a SAFE-designated Chinese tier-1 bank. The SWIFT MT103 instruction must reference the JV name, the SAFE FDI registration QR code, and the SAFE purpose code for foreign direct investment equity contribution; the remittance must not be annotated as a loan, current-account trade payment or personal transfer. After receipt, the JV may apply to the bank for foreign-exchange settlement into RMB supported by genuine operational documentation, and must obtain a capital contribution verification report from a Chinese certified public accountant before the settled funds are deployed. The capital account is monitored by SAFE, and settled RMB can only be used for lawful registered capital purposes with invoice and contract evidence retained on file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For this AdTech JV, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for overseas media, vendor and platform settlement payments, and the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) for cross-border RMB payments when counterparties accept RMB. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections remain available for ancillary physical trade involving hardware, servers or data-centre equipment, though they are not core to the programmatic advertising flow. Every outbound disbursement must be matched to a signed service contract, a commercial invoice, tax withholding proof where required, and the correct SAFE trade or service foreign-exchange purpose code, with the bank completing authenticity verification before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD and RMB/EUR deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts with a licensed Chinese commercial bank, capped at genuine current-account receipts and payments and supported by underlying trade or service contracts.

Onshore foreign-exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps between RMB and USD/EUR for treasury liquidity matching, limited to the JV's actual operational cash-flow exposure and reported to SAFE by the bank.
RMB option products purchased from a licensed onshore bank to hedge existing periods of FX risk; speculative net option selling is not permitted.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps approved by PBOC and SAFE rules for balance-sheet hedging, provided the notional does not exceed the underlying debt or investment exposure.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for a mainland-domiciled JV; the regulatory boundary requires all onshore hedging instruments to be deliverable, exposure-based and executed through a licensed domestic bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June for the preceding calendar year; reporting window is 1 January through 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing causes inclusion in the Operating Exception List; failure to remove the entity from that list within three years transfers it to the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, triggering cross-departmental joint punishment and credit restrictions, and the business license may be revoked for dormancy exceeding six consecutive months under the PRC Company Law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the integrated national foreign investment information reporting system connected to SAMR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June for the preceding calendar year; same 1 January through 30 June window as the enterprise annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOFCOM issues a correction order; failure to correct may result in administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Law and the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures, inclusion in the enterprise credit abnormality record, and joint credit punitive measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Final Settlement and Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) in-charge tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, filing and payment must be completed by 31 May of the following tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, increasing to RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 for serious cases; daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax from the day after the deadline; understated tax may attract penalties ranging from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under the Tax Collection Administration Law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statement Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Prepared for the shareholders and board; retained at the registered office; available to SAMR and the STA on request; performed by a PRC-licensed CPA firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the annual shareholders general meeting date as fixed in the articles of association, and in all events no later than 31 May following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete the statutory annual audit violates the PRC Company Law and Accounting Law; SAMR may order rectification, unaudited financial statements may be rejected by tax and banking authorities, and shareholders or regulators may bring enforcement proceedings that expose the entity and responsible officers to administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Information Confirmation and Amendment Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR through the Beneficial Owner Information filing module and National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing on establishment; for existing entities governed by the 2024 Beneficial Owner Information Measures, initial filing completed by 1 February 2025; thereafter every beneficial ownership change or shareholding control change must be filed within 30 days, and annual confirmation is embedded in the 1 January through 30 June annual enterprise report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false beneficial-owner reporting may trigger administrative warnings and RMB-denominated monetary penalties under the enterprise credit information and anti-money-laundering regimes, inclusion in abnormal-operations or dishonest-institution records, and liability for the directly responsible person.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: PRC law does not provide a size-based exemption; every company, including a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture limited liability entity, must have its annual financial statements independently audited by a PRC-registered CPA firm at each fiscal year-end regardless of balance-sheet assets, turnover, or headcount. The applicable trigger is therefore the existence of a registered corporate entity as of the reporting date. Additional quantitative triggers include: listed issuers must comply with CSRC securities audit rules; banking, insurance, and securities licensees are subject to financial-sector prudential audit requirements; and taxpayers with related-party transactions above the RMB 20 million annual documentation threshold must maintain transfer-pricing contemporaneous documentation under STA Announcement No. 16 of 2016, supported by audit-ready financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE / Chinese GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS; small enterprises may apply the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards if they meet the Ministry of Finance threshold criteria, but a foreign-invested JV operating as a programmatic ad-exchange and SSP platform generally applies ASBE. Books and records must be maintained in the Chinese language, and statutory accounting and tax records must be retained for no less than 10 years under the Tax Collection Administration Law and PRC Company Law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the 2024 Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information, the JV must identify the natural persons who ultimately own or control 25% or more of equity or voting rights, or who otherwise exercise actual control; file that information with SAMR; and update it within 30 days after any shareholding transfer or control change. There is no separate standalone annual UBO declaration; the annual enterprise report filed with SAMR between 1 January and 30 June operates as the annual confirmation event for shareholder and control data. Share transfers must also be recorded in the Register of Members and filed with SAMR within 30 days of the transfer; until so recorded, the transferee cannot assert shareholder rights against the company or against third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of shareholders general meetings and board meetings
Minutes of supervisors committee and executive officer resolutions
Equity transfer and equity pledge or charge registration records
Accounting books, vouchers, and statutory financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,500 per annum for a registered address or office-service arrangement in a Tier-1 Chinese city; licensed local compliance agent services typically USD 800 - USD 2,000 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 30,000 per annum depending on turnover, balance-sheet complexity, cross-border and related-party transactions, and selection of a Big Four or mid-tier Chinese CPA firm.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Enterprise Income Tax Law of the PRC, Article 4)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for certified High-New Technology Enterprises; 100% additional super-deduction for eligible R&D expenditures; two-year exemption and three-year 50% reduction for qualified software enterprises; no free-zone tax holiday is available because the registered seat is in mainland China and the AdTech platform must individually satisfy incentive certifications.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (A-Type), main form A100000 with supporting schedules including A105000 Tax Adjustment Items, A105050 Related-Party Transactions, A107012 R&D Super-Deduction and A109000 Tax Credits; filed via the State Taxation Administration e-Tax web portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement, supplemented by quarterly or monthly provisional payments during the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return must be filed within five months after the calendar tax year-end, i.e. by 31 May of the following year; quarterly provisional returns must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from programmatic ad exchange, DSP/SSP transaction fees, demand-side and supply-side platform commissions, data management services, and AdTech subscription fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrue all PRC-source revenue under written contracts with Chinese advertisers and publishers. Do not net offshore data or algorithm costs against gross revenue. Align revenue recognition with PRC Accounting Standards; ensure that no sales proceeds are diverted through foreign bank accounts or offshore SSP shells. Red flags arise where revenue is recorded with zero or negative gross margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of advertising inventory, cloud/data centre services, content delivery network fees, data feed purchases, and platform infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inventory and data purchased from foreign related parties must be priced at arm's length and evidenced by contracts, delivery logs and invoices. If the non-resident SSP is the counterparty, prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation when statutory thresholds are exceeded. Fictitious ad-traffic or fake data purchases are a common audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duty and other deductible tax levies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT is an input/output tax and is not deductible as a cost. Cross-border electronic services supplied into China may trigger VAT obligations; avoid classifying VAT as a CIT-deductible operating expense. Confirm that surcharges are supported by actual VAT payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales commissions, DSP/SSP user acquisition, business development, sales team salaries, promotional and marketing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions paid to offshore agents may be deductible only if services are genuine, priced at arm's length, and do not create a PRC permanent establishment for the offshore payee. Where a foreign agent negotiates contracts in China, PE exposure may arise. Obtain service completion reports and beneficial ownership evidence before remitting commissions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign parent management fees, consultancy fees, legal and professional fees, office rent, staff salaries, and general overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to a non-resident parent are deductible only for actual services received, with proof of benefit to the JV, no duplicate cost allocation, and arm's-length pricing. Unsupported management fees attract adjustment, penalty and withholding exposure. Senior offshore manager visits can create a service PE in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense on loans, bank charges, exchange gains or losses, and financing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to offshore related lenders is subject to thin capitalisation: the deductible debt-to-equity ratio is generally 2:1. Excess interest is treated as non-deductible and may be recharacterised as a deemed dividend subject to 10% withholding tax. Interest computations and lender substance documentation must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Line 7 - Total Profit and Tax Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before tax as computed from the accounting results, adjusted by Schedule A105000 for non-deductible items, tax-exempt income, and timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply strict PRC source rules when reconciling. Non-resident related-party allocations, excessive cross-border royalties and undocumented service fees must be added back. Include any withheld transaction taxes and permanent establishment attributable profits in the reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 8 - Corporate Income Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed CIT at 25% on taxable income, reduced by credits, tax loss offsets, provisional payments, and any preferential rates or super-deductions claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The JV is the taxpayer on its worldwide income as a Chinese resident company. The non-resident shareholder is taxable only via withholding on distributions, interest, royalties or service fees. Quarterly provisional payments must not be underpaid materially, or late-payment surcharges apply. Any claim of a 15% high-tech rate must be supported by the advanced technology certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return: Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) Article 62 imposes a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under TCAL Article 32. Under TCAL Article 63, false or fraudulent tax filings carry a civil penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 can lead to fines and imprisonment of up to seven years where the amount evaded exceeds the statutory threshold and represents more than 10% of taxable income. A legal representative with serious outstanding liabilities may be placed on the dishonesty/exit-control list and barred from leaving China.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax under EIT Law Article 37 on dividends paid by a Chinese-resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise; no withholding applies to dividends distributed to a Chinese-resident corporate shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain and submit a Tax Residency Certificate issued by its tax authority; (ii) file a Non-resident Enterprise Tax Treatment Application with the Chinese withholding agent before the dividend remittance; (iii) provide a beneficial ownership declaration and substantive evidence that it has real capacity to hold, control and manage the investment; (iv) cite the specific treaty article and shareholding threshold, typically a 5% rate for holdings of at least 25%; and (v) retain records for a possible post-remittance refund if 10% was withheld. In the absence of a TRC or substance, treaty benefits are denied and the statutory 10% rate plus late interest applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for AdTech algorithms, software and patents paid to a non-resident: statutory 10%; most China DTAs reduce the rate to 5%-10% for beneficial owners. Interest on cross-border intercompany loans: statutory 10%; treaty rates are commonly 5%-10%. Royalties and interest must be supported by registered agreements, economic substance, and arm's-length pricing; excessive related-party interest may be recharacterised as a deemed dividend and lose deductibility.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when annual related-party transactions exceed: RMB 200 million for tangible assets, RMB 100 million for intangible assets, RMB 100 million for financial assets, or RMB 40 million for other related-party services. Master File is required where the ultimate parent MNE group's previous-year consolidated revenue reaches RMB 1 billion; Country-by-Country Report is triggered at consolidated group revenue of RMB 5.5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not impose a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulation, but the tax authorities enforce a substance-over-form doctrine through GAAR under EIT Law Article 47, the DTA beneficial-ownership rule, and special tax adjustment investigations. For a programmatic AdTech JV, the Core Income-Generating Activities must be exercised in China: algorithmic price decision-making, contract negotiation, ad-server operation, risk-bearing, data management, and qualified technical staff. If those functions are performed offshore, treaty relief and arm's-length assumptions may be disregarded and income recharacterised.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Falsified Ad-Tech Costs and Fabricated Transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking fictitious programmatic advertising inventory purchases, inflating data-traffic fees through offshore shell SSPs, creating false invoices for nonexistent DSP services, or routing revenue through foreign bank accounts to understate PRC taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TCAL Article 63: civil penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax; disallowance of all fictitious costs under EIT Law Articles 6-8; Criminal Law Article 201: criminal tax evasion punishable by fine and imprisonment of up to seven years where the evaded amount is large and exceeds the statutory proportion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under PRC Company Law's disregard-of-corporate-personality doctrine, directors who controlled the fraudulent scheme are personally liable for restitution of diverted corporate assets and payment of the evaded tax. The legal representative may be blocked from leaving China through the tax authority's exit-control/dishonest taxpayer list. Willful participation can result in director-level criminal imprisonment and financial penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell/Jurisdiction Treaty Abuse and Beneficial Ownership Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the JV's dividend or royalty stream through a conduit holding company that lacks real employees, premises, board activity, or economic decision-making in the claimed treaty country, solely to obtain a lower DTA withholding rate or a 5% dividend rate under a Chinese bilateral treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and reimposition of the statutory 10% withholding tax; TCAL Article 32 daily late surcharge; EIT Law Article 47 GAAR permits recharacterisation of the conduit arrangement; false beneficial-ownership filings expose the taxpayer to TCAL Article 63 penalties of 50%-500% of the under-withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false tax residency or beneficial-ownership declarations may be jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax through veil piercing. They may be blacklisted with travel bans and asset attachment; criminal prosecution for tax evasion or issuing false tax invoices can impose imprisonment of up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Failure to Maintain Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying offshore parent or SSP affiliates excessive algorithm royalties, data management fees, or interest; failing to prepare Local File/Master File once the RMB thresholds are exceeded; refusing to provide related-party transaction data during an SAT transfer pricing audit or claiming intercompany payments without arm's-length comparability and substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 44 authorises the tax authority to estimate taxable income if documentation is not produced; Article 48 requires unilateral adjustment with interest at the PBOC benchmark lending rate plus five percentage points, and the special tax adjustment may be assessed retroactively. TCAL Articles 62-63 add administrative fines and penalties of 50%-500% of any underpaid tax if the mispricing is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the financial officer who approved the intercompany contracts can be held personally accountable for the corporate tax shortfall when abuse of corporate personality is shown. Recovery includes personal asset seizure, travel restrictions, and blacklisting; criminal liability for tax evasion attaches if they knowingly structured false transfer pricing for the benefit of an offshore related party.
